commentary.text: I claim a central square immediately and establish a Red anchor that can support future sandwiches across row 3.

I’m taking the safer central foothold at (4,4). It contests the center without placing Blue beside the advanced Red piece, where Red could soon form a sandwich; Green can later support the neighboring center square or build a capture threat.
I reinforce Red’s central foothold with Yellow, claiming a second center square and restricting Green’s access along row 4.

I’m advancing Green to (4,2), reinforcing Blue’s central foothold and pressuring Yellow at (4,3). The aligned cluster limits Yellow’s easy horizontal options while preparing Green to contest the lower central squares.
I’m reinforcing our central wedge with Red, occupying a third center square and restricting Blue’s access through column 4.

I’m exploiting the vertical Blue–Red–Blue alignment: moving to (2,4) sandwiches and captures Red at (3,4), breaking Team A’s control of the upper center while preserving Blue’s occupation of (4,4). Yellow can attack that Blue piece next, but it can no longer complete an immediate four-square center victory.
I’m using Yellow’s advanced center piece as the far flank: landing on (4,5) sandwiches and captures Blue at (4,4), removing its central foothold while preserving our Red–Yellow center structure.

I’m withdrawing the exposed Green from (4,2), which Yellow could sandwich next turn by landing at (4,1). Repositioning to (2,2) keeps Green active near the center while avoiding an immediate Red or Yellow capture.
I’m staging a second Red beside the upper center. This preserves Red’s hold on (3,3) and threatens to complete the top-center pair on a later Red turn while Yellow works on the lower center.

I’m restoring Blue to the open center at (4,4). This blocks Team A from assembling the four central squares and clears (2,4) for Green’s future development, while the existing Yellow pair on row 4 cannot capture Blue without first breaking and later rebuilding its formation.
I’m tightening the Yellow formation around the central Blue piece, restricting its movement and preparing a future enclosure while keeping our center presence intact.

I’m placing Green at (2,3) to create a forcing vertical threat: next Green turn, the piece at (5,0) can land on (5,3), sandwiching and capturing both Yellow at (4,3) and Red at (3,3). Team A must break that alignment, likely surrendering some central control.
I’m tightening our central formation: Red joins its partner at (3,3), giving Team A three of the four center squares while keeping the Blue piece at (4,4) under sustained pressure.

I’m creating a fork around the center. Blue now threatens to land at (4,6), capturing Yellow at (4,5) against the Blue anchor at (4,4). Yellow must also answer Green’s pending (5,3) sandwich of Yellow (4,3) and Red (3,3), so Team A cannot save both targets with one move.

Yellow drives into (4,6), using the Yellow anchor at (4,3) to sandwich both Blue pieces on the central row. This immediately inflicts Blue’s second and third losses, eliminating Blue and clearing the contested center squares.

I’m executing the prepared Green sandwich: landing at (5,3) uses Green at (2,3) as the far anchor, capturing Yellow at (4,3) and Red at (3,3). This inflicts losses on both enemy colors, leaves Red one capture from elimination, and weakens Team A’s center.
I develop a second Red piece toward the center while keeping the Red piece on (3,4) in place. This prepares (3,3) for Red and restricts Green’s approach along row 3.

I’m using Blue’s center anchor at (4,4) to sandwich Yellow at (5,4). Landing at (6,4) scores Yellow’s second loss, protects Green at (5,3) from Yellow’s planned horizontal capture, and leaves Yellow one loss from elimination.

I’m placing Yellow on the fourth rank to exploit Green’s looming capture on Red. If Green enters (4,3), Yellow will threaten a mixed-line sandwich through Green and the central Blue piece, forcing the opponent to disrupt that formation.

I’m occupying (3,3) to secure a second central square and threaten Red’s last life: Green at (3,0) can next land on (3,1), sandwiching Red at (3,2) against this new anchor. Red must disrupt that threat instead of advancing its center plan.

I’m lifting the central Red piece briefly, threatening to return to (3,2) and sandwich the Green piece on (3,3) against Red on (3,4). This should force Green to abandon a central square while keeping Red safe.

I’m sidestepping the threatened Blue center piece to (4,3). This preserves two Team B central squares and threatens to return to (4,4), sandwiching both Yellow pieces against Blue at (4,7) and eliminating Yellow; Yellow must now break that line.
I’m using Yellow’s aligned pair to sandwich the Blue piece on (4,3), raising Blue to two losses and clearing a central square for a future center takeover.

I’m shifting Green to (2,3) to threaten Red’s final loss: Green can next land at (2,1), sandwiching Red at (2,2) against the Green anchor at (2,3). Red must answer this threat, while Blue still threatens to return to (4,4) and capture both Yellow pieces on row 4, eliminating Yellow.
I’m occupying the threatened central square at (4,4), preventing Blue from moving there and sandwiching both Yellow pieces against the Blue piece on the right edge.
I’m repositioning the confirmed Blue anchor from (4,7) to the open square at (3,7), keeping it mobile after the central Blue was removed.
I’m clearing (4,2) so Red can potentially land there and sandwich the Blue piece on (4,3) against Red on (4,4). Keeping Yellow on (4,1) avoids exposing it to an immediate Green sandwich.

I’m executing Green’s prepared sandwich at (2,1), capturing Red at (2,2) against the Green anchor at (2,3). This is Red’s third loss, eliminating Red and converting its remaining pieces to Void; Team B now needs only one more Yellow capture to eliminate Team A entirely.

The central Red Void piece must leave the fourth row to break Blue’s looming sandwich through the two Yellow pieces. Moving it upward preserves a central foothold while preventing immediate Yellow elimination.

I’m restoring Blue’s far anchor at (4,7), creating an immediate elimination threat: Blue can next land at (4,4), sandwiching both Yellow pieces at (4,5) and (4,6). Yellow must move the outer piece at (4,6) vertically to break the line, since moving the inner piece would still leave the outer Yellow capturable between Blue’s pieces.
I bring the isolated Yellow piece up to complete a same-color sandwich around Blue at (4,3), raising Blue to two losses while consolidating the fourth row.

I’m establishing Green at (4,0), the far anchor for a second elimination threat. If Red’s Void at (3,4) blocks Blue’s planned landing on (4,4), Blue can vacate (4,3), allowing Green at (5,3) to land there later and sandwich the two left-side Yellow pieces against this new anchor.
I reposition a Red Void piece toward the center, preserving Yellow’s opportunity to land on (4,4) and sandwich the Blue piece at (4,3).

I’m completing the decisive Blue sandwich: moving from (4,3) to (4,4) traps both Yellow pieces at (4,5) and (4,6) against Blue at (4,7). Their capture gives Yellow its third loss, eliminating Team A’s remaining color and winning the game.
